requirements.note: Newest first, with an initials avatar, sender, subject, two-line preview and date ('Oct 24', or the time for today). Unread is marked only by a tiny green dot on the avatar; the subject is not bolded, so unread rows are hard to spot.
Swipe left shows Flag and Archive, and a full swipe archives. Swipe right toggles Read/Unread. Archived mail appears on an Archive tab, where swiping offers 'Inbox' to move it back.
Flag from the swipe or from the reader toolbar; a flag icon appears under the avatar. A segmented All/Unread/Flagged filter works (23 flagged, 109 unread).
Tapping pushes a reader with subject, sender, full date and body; the unread count drops. The reader toolbar has archive, flag and mark-unread.
Pulling down adds two new unread messages at the top with the current time. It also works from the options menu (Refresh Inbox).
'320 messages · 109 unread' sits under the filter, and the Inbox tab shows a badge with the count.
After a relaunch the read, unread, flagged and archived states were kept, and so were the refreshed messages.

bugs: After a pull to refresh, the list stays scrolled with the large title collapsed into a small 'Inbox' instead of springing back to the top.
Accessibility tree carries dozens of stale off-screen text elements stacked at one point, which VoiceOver could read out.
tells: The floating tab bar (Inbox/Archive with badge) is drawn by hand: its items have no accessibility labels, so they can only be tapped by position.
The segmented filter is a custom green pill control, not the system segmented control look.
Unread is shown by a tiny green dot on the avatar instead of Mail's blue dot and bold text.
The green accent colour throughout makes it look like a brand app rather than system blue.
The search field stays pinned and floats over the list with blur after scrolling, instead of tucking under the navigation bar.
Swipe actions are circular buttons with captions underneath, not full-height swipe-action panels.
The reader toolbar is three separate circular buttons; at large text the body is cut off hard under them.
Rows are tall (about 119pt) with lots of spacing, so few messages fit on a screen compared with Mail.
A.scroll: A slow drag tracks the finger; flings decelerate naturally and flinging back reaches the top with the large title restored. I saw no blank or popping rows. The scroll position after returning from a message shifted by about 50pt.

requirements.note: Newest first with sender, subject, two-line preview and a Mail-style date (time today, then weekday, then M/D/YY). Unread rows have a blue dot and a bold subject, as in Mail.

Swipe left shows Flag and Archive, and a full swipe archives. Swipe right shows Unread/Read. An Archive screen, opened from a navigation-bar button, lists archived mail with an 'Inbox' swipe to move it back.

Flag from the swipe or from the reader's navigation bar; an orange flag shows at the row's trailing edge. A filter pull-down menu offers All Messages, Unread and Flagged, and the section header shows the count ('Flagged · 23').
Tapping pushes a reader with subject, sender, 'To: me', date and body, plus a 'Mark as Unread' button; opening marks the message read (the count drops).
Pulling down adds two new unread messages at the top ('Alex Morgan', 'Maya Chen'). Refresh is also in the filter menu.
'109 unread' appears as a subtitle under the large title, and in the inline title once scrolled.
After a relaunch the read, flagged and archived states and the new messages were kept.

bugs: The push into a message feels slow: it was still mid-slide about 0.5 s after the tap and only just settled by about 0.9 s.
Accessibility labels on the rows leave out the unread and flagged state, so VoiceOver gives no unread information.
tells: Every mail row has a disclosure chevron, which Mail does not show.
At the largest text size, the sender name is squeezed beside the date and wraps to three lines ('Alex / Mor- / gan') instead of the row stacking.
The swipe actions are circular buttons with captions, and the swiped row is drawn as a grey rounded card rather than system full-height actions.
There is no search in the inbox.
The 'Mark as Unread' control in the reader is an inline link-style button in the body rather than in a toolbar.
B.scroll: Slow drags track well, and flings decelerate and run smoothly with a sticky section header and an inline title that blurs content beneath it. I saw no blank rows or popping. Flinging back reaches the top with the large title, and the scroll position after returning from a message was kept within about 10pt.

why: Both apps meet every requirement, and their swipe actions and persistence behave almost the same. B reads more like Apple Mail: blue unread dots with bold subjects, a filter pull-down in the navigation bar, Mail-style relative dates and trailing flag marks. A has a hand-drawn floating tab bar and green pill control, and its unread marker is weak. A does have search and a better large-text row layout, but B is the one I would rather use and ship.
